title: Forensic lab report delays - impact on NDPS trials
p1:
A case can look strong in court… yet a delayed forensic report can change everything.

Many people assume that once drugs are seized, a conviction is almost automatic. But the scientific confirmation of the substance often becomes the turning point in an NDPS trial.
p2:
A surprising fact: the seized material alone may not always be enough. The forensic lab report helps establish what the substance actually is and whether it falls under the category covered by the law.

When reports are delayed, trials may slow down, evidence may remain unconfirmed, and courts have to carefully examine whether the accused's rights are being affected.
p3:
For investigators, timely laboratory analysis is not just a procedural step—it can decide the strength of the entire case. For the accused, unnecessary delays can raise concerns about a fair and speedy trial.

The practical lesson is simple: in NDPS matters, science and law must move together. A strong investigation needs both proper seizure procedures and timely expert verification.
